edges.reason: Constructor assigns owner from msg.sender, so ownership depends on the caller.
onlyOwner modifier reads the owner state variable for comparison.
onlyOwner requires msg.sender == owner before transferOwnership executes.
newOwner is the input argument of transferOwnership.
transferOwnership writes newOwner into the owner state variable.
set_amount is protected by the onlyOwner modifier reading owner.
Privileged set_amount is gated by msg.sender == owner.
new_amount is multiplied by 10**18 in an unchecked arithmetic operation.
Result of new_amount*10**18 is stored into amount.
set_address is protected by the onlyOwner modifier reading owner.
Privileged set_address is gated by msg.sender == owner.
new_address is written into the tokenAddress state variable.
set_cooldown is protected by the onlyOwner modifier reading owner.
Privileged set_cooldown is gated by msg.sender == owner.
new_cooldown is written into the cooldown state variable.
withdraw is protected by the onlyOwner modifier reading owner.
Privileged withdraw is gated by msg.sender == owner.
withdraw multiplies the caller-supplied _amount by 10**18.
Scaled _amount becomes the value of the external token transfer.
tokenAddress is used to instantiate ERC20Basic for the transfer.
owner is the recipient of the withdrawn tokens.
External ERC20 call can hand control to an arbitrary token contract and re-enter withdraw.
Fallback function forwards to play_game(0).
play_paper calls play_game(0).
play_scissors calls play_game(1).
play_stone calls play_game(2).
msg.sender indexes readyTime, record and is the payout recipient in play_game.
block.timestamp is used in the cooldown requirement of play_game.
readyTime[msg.sender] is read for the cooldown requirement.
play argument drives the game logic in play_game.
block.timestamp seeds the keccak256 pseudo-random computer move.
play_game computes the computer move from block values.
Randomness output modulo 3 is assigned to the comp local variable.
play_game calls compare(play, comp) to obtain the result.
Player move is passed into compare.
Computed computer move is passed into compare.
compare reads its player parameter.
compare reads its computer parameter.
compare writes the outcome into its _result local variable.
Result of compare becomes the result local in play_game.
result is multiplied by 9 when packing the record.
play is multiplied by 3 when packing the record.
comp is added when packing the record value.
msg.sender is used as the record mapping index.
Packed value is stored into record[msg.sender].
play_game performs the prize token transfer when the player wins.
tokenAddress is used to instantiate ERC20Basic for the payout.
amount is the value transferred to the winning player.
msg.sender is the recipient of the payout, influenced by the caller.
External token transfer can re-enter play_game before state is finalized, and randomness relies on miner-controlled values.
block.timestamp is added to the cooldown on a loss.
cooldown is added to the current timestamp.
Computed timestamp is written back to readyTime[msg.sender].
orig parameter is divided and reduced modulo to unpack fields.
judge performs unchecked division and modulo operations.
orig/9 produces the decoded result field.
(orig%9)/3 produces the decoded play field.
orig%3 produces the decoded comp field.
resolve calls judge to decode the packed record.
resolve passes its orig argument into judge.
Decoded result is passed to win for string conversion.
win reads its _result parameter.
resolve calls win to format the outcome.
Decoded play move is passed to mora.
Decoded computer move is passed to mora.
resolve calls mora twice to format the moves.
mora reads its orig parameter.
view_last_result indexes the record mapping with the supplied address.
view_last_result reads the stored record value.
Caller-supplied address drives the record lookup.
view_last_result calls resolve to format the record.
self_last_result uses msg.sender as the queried address.
self_last_result forwards to view_last_result.
view_readyTime reads readyTime for the supplied address.
view_readyTime compares block.timestamp against the stored ready time.
Stored ready time is used to compute the remaining cooldown.
Caller-supplied address drives the readyTime lookup.
self_readyTime uses msg.sender as the queried address.
self_readyTime forwards to view_readyTime.
